newsitem.title: USA: U.S. uninsured rate at 17 percent - study.
newsitem.headline: U.S. uninsured rate at 17 percent - study.

text.p: Up to 17 percent of Americans lacked health insurance early in 1996, according to preliminary federal data released Thursday.

The data released from the Agency for Health Care Policy and Research did not say how many millions of people that translated into, but other recent studies have estimated about 40 million are uninsured.

"The data we release today provide a 'first look' set of estimates for the number of uninsured Americans in 1996," said the agency's administrator Dr. John Eisenberg. He said the final numbers may be smaller when the agency finalizes its study of uninsured Americans for last year.
The survey found that 19 percent of men, and 15 percent of women, were uninsured. Uninsurance rates were higher in the South and West than the North and East.
Hispanics had the highest uninsurance rate of any group, more than one in three.

The agency uses slightly different methodology, and comes up with a slightly higher rate, than the Census Bureau and some other federal surveys but the overall picture will be similar once the final data for the year is compiled, he said.
President Clinton in 1993-94 tried to enact universal health insurance but the proposal died in Congress, the biggest domestic policy setback of his first term.
